Al-Rahman: one of the Beautiful Names of Allah, and it belongs to the attribute of mercy (rahma). It means bestowing blessings, even on one who does not deserve them. For this reason we were taught to say, when we begin our actions, "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful" (bismillah al-rahman al-rahim), because you may be a disobedient person and feel shy to begin a work in the name of One you disobey. So it is said to you: say it, for I am al-Rahman.

Intensification in mercy (al-mubalagha fi al-rahma) comes in two senses: intensification in the attribute itself, meaning vast mercy; and intensification that comes from the multiplicity of mercies through the multiplicity of those who receive mercy, meaning: no mercy suffices without another mercy.

This is the meaning of al-Rahman, that His mercy encompasses the believer and the disbeliever alike, since He withholds nothing from one who takes the means. As He, glorified is He, said: ﴿Whoever desires the tilth of the Hereafter, We increase for him in his tilth; and whoever desires the tilth of this world, We give him of it, but he has no share in the Hereafter﴾ [al-Shura: 20]. Thus the disobedient and the disbelievers enjoy blessings in this world under the shelter of the word "al-Rahman."

So: the Truth, glorified is He, is Rahman of this world, while al-Rahim is for the Hereafter. Therefore they say: "Al-Rahman of the world, al-Rahim of the Hereafter," because His mercy in the Hereafter is attained only by the believer, and the disbeliever has no share in it.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah 55, verse 2

It is remarkable that the Truth, glory be to Him, mentioned the teaching of the Qur'an (2) before the creation of man (3), to teach us the importance of knowledge and of laying down the methods and foundations before we proceed to action. Before He created man, He laid down for him the method of his life, like one who manufactures a product and provides for it the "catalogue" (manual) that guarantees its maintenance. We see that a machine breaks down and is corrupted when it is not used according to the method that keeps it in order. Likewise, man is not afflicted with ruin except when he opposes the method of his Lord.

So: "the teaching of the Qur'an (2) the creation of man (3)" means that the laying down of the method preceded the creation of man. Man came and found the method that defines for him: do this and do not do that, this is lawful and this is unlawful, this is good and this is evil.

Among the meanings of mercy (rahmah) in the Qur'an is that the one who shows mercy cares for the one shown mercy in a way that preserves for him the essentials of his life, in a soundness free of defect and ruin. Therefore He, the Exalted, says: ﴿And We send down of the Qur'an that which is a healing and a mercy for the believers﴾ (17:82). They said: it is a healing for the disease that befalls you as a result of heedlessness of the method, and mercy is that the disease does not occur in the first place...

Then we pause at another meaning of "the Merciful" (al-Rahman) in His saying: ﴿Say: Call upon Allah or call upon the Merciful﴾ (17:110). He brought the attribute of mercy after the attribute of divinity, because divinity entails obligation (taklif), and obligation may be burdensome to the soul, so it was fitting that the attribute of mercy be mentioned after it.

It is as if He, the Exalted, were saying to you: do not be anxious, for the One who imposed the obligation upon you is the Merciful, whose mercy embraces all things, and whose mercifulness (rahmaniyyah) encompasses the believer and the disbeliever alike.

On the matter of the beginning of creation, He, the Exalted, said: ﴿He who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, then established Himself upon the Throne—the Merciful; so ask about Him one who is informed﴾ (25:59).

So the Truth, glory be to Him, after creating the creation, established Himself upon His Throne. Istiwa' means dominion and the settling of affairs in His favour, glory be to Him. Here He mentions the attribute of mercy to tell us: this is not a dominion of coercion, oppression and tyranny, but a dominion of mercifulness.

Even in the standing of the Hereafter, with its terrors, He mentions the attribute of mercy: ﴿There is none in the heavens and the earth but that he comes to the Merciful as a servant﴾ (19:93). He, glory be to Him, is tender toward His creation and gives them hope in His compassion and His love for them.

Here "the Merciful" (al-Rahman) came as an independent verse, ﴿The Merciful﴾ (55:1), because when it is uttered it does not refer except to the Truth, glory be to Him, and it gathers all these meanings and their flowing current which runs through every obligation.

Regarding the placement of the teaching of the Qur'an (2) before the creation of man (3), the scholars discussed the question of the end (ghayah) and the means (wasilah): which of the two precedes the other? It is commonly known that the end comes after the means. If you want to go, for example, to Alexandria, you ride a means of transport and take a road that brings you to it, and by using the means you reach your end, which is Alexandria.

Yes, human beings are unable to know ends in advance, but the Lord of human beings knows them in advance and from eternity; He informs you of your end before you are created and before the means leads you to it. Accordingly, ends may be placed before means. We say: you did not take the road to Alexandria except while it was in your mind; the end existed before the means.

And we may combine the two opinions by saying that the end comes first as planning, because you determine the end before beginning the means, while the means comes first as actuality and execution. So: "the teaching of the Qur'an (2)" is the means that brings us to the desired end. Thus the means is after the end in planning, but the end is after the means in actuality. Or, to put it another way: the end is before the means as motive, but it comes after the means in actuality.

The whole Qur'an aims at creed ('aqa'id), rulings (ahkam), manners (adab) and narratives (qisas). The core of creed is in the heart: that we believe in one God, the One, the Unique, and that we associate nothing with Him. This faith has two wings: fear and hope. So when you are in good, security and safety, do not feel safe from the plotting of God; and when you are in hardship and misery, do not despair of the mercy of God.

If the heart is steeped in this sound creed, it pumps it to the rest of the limbs, so the conduct of the limbs comes into accord with the creed of the heart.

When you follow the rulings, commands and manners of the Qur'an, you find the mercifulness (rahmaniyyah) of "the Merciful" flowing generally through all the limbs. The first limb in obligation is the tongue, then the ear, because the tongue is the conveyer and the ear is the receiver, and the first reception from God must be characterised by truthfulness and trustworthiness, since he is a conveyer on behalf of God.

Therefore we say in praise of our master, the Messenger of God: "Peace and blessings be upon you, O my master, O Messenger of God; O ear of good that received the last of the heavenly messages; and O tongue of truth that conveyed the Truth's intent to creation."

God prepared His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) for this mission and placed in him the qualities of receiving and conveying that qualify him for it. His people bore witness to him even before his mission, and we see that those who hastened to believe in Muhammad before they saw a miracle supporting him believed in him because of their prior knowledge of his conduct and character.

Therefore, when God made him known to his people, He said to them: ﴿Muhammad is the Messenger of God﴾ (48:29). That is: this Muhammad whom you know and to whom you bear witness, about whose truthfulness and trustworthiness you do not disagree, is the Messenger of God to you. So the word "Muhammad" and his very name are themselves the ground of his being the Messenger of God.

The Qur'anic method is the "user manual" (dalil al-isti'mal) that sets right the movement of human life. It has come with what preserves the tongue: it commands you to remember God and speak the truth, and forbids you from speaking falsehood, vanity and idle talk. And with what preserves the ear: it commands you to listen to what is good and beneficial for your life, and forbids you from listening to falsehood...

Thus you find that the Qur'anic method preserves for you all the limbs through what it has made clear to you of the lawful and the unlawful, the good that it commands you to do, and the evil it forbids you from. When you reflect on these commands and prohibitions, you see that they are a manifestation of God's mercy towards us, and you find the flow of mercifulness in all of them.

So if the movement of life stands according to the method of God, justice and prosperity prevail, and every possessor of a right is given his right; but if it stands on other than this method, rights are lost, corruption spreads and honour is violated...

So we say: the flow of "the Merciful" is in all the rulings and in the whole method, even in His command of retribution (qisas), that the murderer is killed. Even in killing there is mercy, for it protects the murderer, protects the murdered, and protects the whole society: had the murderer known that he would be killed, he would not have dared to kill.

All the legal obligations proceed from this mercifulness since God created Adam, peace be upon him, and settled him in Paradise, and made for him this training trial in submission to command. When Adam abided by the command of obedience, he settled in Paradise and enjoyed it; when he opposed the command, he was made wretched, his nakedness appeared and his condition became evil.

From this trial we learned the stance of Satan toward man, and we must take a lesson from the lesson that our father Adam lived, and beware of opposing the method of God.

And recite: ﴿He said: Go down from it, all of you, some of you enemies to others. Then when guidance comes to you from Me, whoever follows My guidance will neither go astray nor suffer. But whoever turns away from My remembrance, indeed he will have a depressed life, and We will gather him on the Day of Resurrection blind.﴾ He will say: ﴿My Lord, why have You gathered me blind, while I was [formerly] seeing?﴾ He will say: ﴿Thus Our signs came to you, but you forgot them; and similarly, today you are forgotten.﴾ (20:123–126).

So: the entire obligation came flowing with mercifulness, and even in the case of departing from the method and the occurrence of opposition, your Lord does not abandon you, and this mercy does not leave you. Rather, He legislates repentance for you and opens for you the door of return to His presence, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills...﴾ (4:48). Thus the legislation of repentance itself is from the flow of mercifulness.

Then Allah, glorified is He, commanded us to establish the balance of justice: ﴿That you not transgress in the balance﴾. Transgression (al-tughyan) is exceeding the limit; that is, do not go beyond truth into falsehood. So the verses speak to us of a cosmic system founded on truth and on a precise order that neither deviates nor fails.

The balance of justice governs the movement of the sun and the moon just as it governs human movement. Recite: ﴿Neither is it for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day, and each in an orbit is swimming﴾ [Ya-Sin: 40]. Thus nothing transgresses upon anything else, and so it is with the human being.

﴿That you not transgress in the balance﴾. The celestial bodies and orbits, when they stood firm upon what they were created for and upon the purpose of Allah in them, their movement remained steady in performing their task in the universe, so we do not see, for example, any collision among these bodies. Likewise, O human being, if you wish for the movement of your life to be upright, then walk in it by this balance which Allah has set for you.

Allah, the Truth, glorified is He, said about the sky: ﴿And the sky He raised high﴾ (al-Rahman 55:7). And He said about the earth: ﴿He laid it down﴾... That is, He made it low and spread out. He, glorified is He, said: ﴿Who made the earth a cradle﴾ (Ta-Ha 20:53), so it is smoothed out, and He said: ﴿Have We not made the earth a bed?﴾ (al-Naba 78:6). It bears the human being as a cradle bears the infant. The earth was laid down so that the human being might settle upon it.

The meaning of ﴿for the creatures﴾ (lil-anam) is for the children of Adam. Others said: rather, the anam includes every living thing (kull dhi ruh), so animals in this sense are among the anam, because they eat from the earth's produce and live upon it. And they said: the jinn too are among the anam.

We note in this verse the generality regarding "the earth," for it does not specify "a particular earth." This indicates comprehensiveness: the earth means every earth, in every place, and likewise the anam means every kind of creature. So God's earth is in every place, for the servants of God in every place.

We understand this meaning from His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Those whose souls the angels take while they are wronging themselves, the angels will say: "In what state were you?" They will say: "We were oppressed in the earth." The angels will say: "Was not the earth of Allah spacious enough for you to migrate therein?" For those, their refuge is Hell, and evil is the destination﴾ (al-Nisa 4:97).

So God's earth belongs to everyone. If life becomes constricted for you here, go to another place where there is room. This alone, if they acted upon it, would be sufficient to resolve the problems of the world today. But what has happened is that they have severed the joints of this natural unity which the Creator intended for creation, and they have placed between themselves borders and barriers.

It is strange that we see them disputing over a few meters of their borders, while they live across hundreds, indeed thousands, of kilometers of Allah's earth. Then, if you contemplate the map and see how the borders between countries are drawn now, do you see them in the shape of a straight line?

No, rather they are winding, crooked, and interlocked with one another. Thus did the Real, glorified is He, intend them: the earth, all of it, is for the creatures, all of them.

We now see lands that nearly burst from the multitude of their population, yet they have few resources, and on the contrary, we see lands empty of people, full of neglected resources that no one finds to extract them. Is this the just balance upon which the affairs of creation stand? No, by Allah, rather this is injustice and tyranny in the balance.

And you may look at the artificial borders, the walls, the airports, the gates, and the strict laws that govern them, and the visas and conditions, to the point that you spend a month or months preparing papers and visas so that you may be able to enter such-and-such a country.

Then there followed from this separation by borders international disputes, racial discrimination, and the monopolization of wealth by its owners, so wars and conflicts arose, as you see.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 55, verse 13:

﴿Then which of the favours of your Lord would you both deny?﴾ The address is to the two weighty groups (al-thaqalan), the jinn and mankind. For this reason He will address them afterwards: ﴿We will soon attend to you, O two weighty ones﴾ (31). Here the Truth, glory be to Him, addresses them with this interrogation: these are the blessings and favours of Allah. So which of these blessings will you both deny, O mankind and O jinn?

Among the methods of the Noble Qur'an is that when the Truth, glory be to Him, wants to establish a ruling and emphasise it, He does not present it in the form of a statement, but in the form of a question, as if He were saying to them: say it yourselves, and we are seeking the answer. The answer to the question must be: "And none of Your blessings, our Lord, do we deny."

When you follow the path of a question, you are only doing so while confident that the answer will come, without fail, as you wish. Like someone who denies your favour upon him, so you say to him: "Did I not do such-and-such for you?"

The word ālā' (آلاء)... meaning blessings, the plural of ìl (إلى) in the sense of ḥiml and aḥmāl (a plural pattern). This verse ﴿Then which of the favours of your Lord would you both deny?﴾ is repeated in this surah many times, and this has a distinction and a wisdom, as in His saying in the surah before it: ﴿And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?﴾ (17) [al-Qamar], and similarly ﴿Then how was My punishment and warning?﴾ (21) [al-Fajr]. Such repetition has a wisdom: it adds something new, otherwise it would be mere excess, and the Qur'an is free of this.

So the method, when it repeats ﴿Then which of the favours of your Lord would you both deny?﴾, is a foundation for each particular blessing. With each blessing this method recurs, making each blessing separately the subject of this question.

This verse has been repeated in Surat al-Rahman thirty-one times, for the Truth, glory be to Him, wanted to affirm to us the flow of divine mercy (al-Rahmaniyyah) in Surat al-Rahman, mentioning it with every blessing: "Will you deny such-and-such?" And how could we deny while we live in this bliss night and day?

This means that when we listen to the Qur'an, we must be moved by it and reflect on its meaning, not let it pass over our ears as it would any other human speech. We have seen people of faith and closeness to Allah doing this: when the name of Allah is mentioned, they say "Subhanallah" or "Jalla Jalaluh"; when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is mentioned, they say: "Sallallahu 'alayhi wa sallam." When Paradise is mentioned, they ask for it; when the Fire is mentioned, they seek refuge in Allah from it. Thus the believer interacts with the words of Allah, so where are we from those people?

It is remarkable that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) should report this, when he had never sailed the sea and did not know this type of ship. The ships that existed in the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) were small, flat, and single-decked, and multi-decked ships were not known until the eighteenth century CE. Thus, this verse is part of the miraculous nature of the Qur'an and one of the signs of prophethood, and a proof of the truthfulness of the Prophet (ﷺ) in reporting and conveying from Allah.
